source: Belova et al., arXiv:2501.03425, 'Hybrid simulations of FRC merging and compression' (HYM)

cases.name: fig1_merge
cases.observed_time_note: peak reconnection at t ~ 5 tA; the FRCs merge only partially into a doublet (final ΔZ ≈ 40 MHD, ≈ 90 hybrid), so this is not a completed-merge time

cases.name: fig3_4_merge
cases.observed_time_note: midpoint of the hybrid range t ~ 6-7 tA (nearly complete merging); the MHD run merges completely by t ~ 5 tA; the printed separation is ΔZ ≈ 75

cases.name: fig5_no_merge_dz185
cases.observed_time_note: printed as ΔZ ≈ 185; the FRCs reach ΔZ ≈ 140 by t ~ 50 tA and then drift apart

cases.name: compression_merge
cases.observed_time_note: same initial FRCs as Figs 1-2, starting at ΔZ ≈ 180 with Vz ≈ 0 (Fig 8) and driven by the mirror field to Vz ~ 0.4 vA at t ≈ 10 tA; fully merged at t ~ 20-25 tA (midpoint 22.5)

notes: Merge/no-merge is decided by the real MIF MergeWindowMonitor driven by Belova-normalized initial conditions; the monitor's first-lock time tracks the ballistic closure.

Ballistic closure is a kinematic reference, not a bound: reconnection_speedup divides it by the printed time named in observed_time_note; it is above 1 for Fig 1 (peak reconnection in a partial merge, ~2.4), Figs 3-4 and Fig 5 at dZ=110, and below 1 for Fig 5 at dZ=125, where the FRCs merge later than the closure. Acceleration and drag are FUSION-owned (FUS-C.6, ADR 0001).

Compression cases are excluded from the kinematic classification and get no ballistic or monitor number: they start at rest and the increasing mirror field that drives them is FUSION-owned physics, not MIF kinematics.
tau_window_tA is a single calibrated threshold; the data bound it to the open interval in tau_window_bound_tA.
